title: Game Stats Page
statement: A game keeps each player's coins per day for 10 years (3,650 days). The stats page answers about 1,000,000 "coins from day a to day b" questions a day; the coin history never changes.

approaches.name: Build running totals once, answer each question with one subtraction
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One pass to build, then O(1) per question.

approaches.name: Add up the days for each question
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but up to 3.65 billion additions a day.

approaches.name: Cache the answer to each question asked before
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Helps only when the same ranges repeat.

approaches.name: Return the overall total
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Answers the wrong question for any range shorter than all days.

title: Ledger Stretches
statement: An accountant has 200,000 daily balance changes (positive or negative) and must count how many stretches of consecutive days changed the balance by exactly $0.

approaches.name: Running total with a hash map of how often each total appeared
approaches.hint: Equal totals mean a zero stretch
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: A stretch sums to 0 exactly when two running totals are equal.

approaches.name: Prefix array, then compare every pair of totals
approaches.label: valid

approaches.name: A sliding window that shrinks when the sum is too big
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: With negative values the sum does not change predictably, so the window misses stretches.

title: Population Map Tiles
statement: A census map is a 2,000 × 2,000 grid of population counts. A planning tool asks for the total population inside 50,000 different rectangles.

approaches.name: A 2D prefix-sum table; each rectangle is four lookups
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Build once, then O(1) per rectangle.

approaches.name: Prefix sums per row; add one range per row
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, up to 2,000 steps per rectangle.

approaches.name: Add every cell of each rectangle
approaches.label: valid

approaches.name: Estimate from a sample of cells
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Fast, but the totals must be exact.
